headline: 1997 executive order on whether certain people who worked for the U.S. government overseas can be hired into federal jobs without competing.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order sets rules for whether certain overseas workers can get federal jobs through a noncompetitive appointment. This means they could be hired without going through the usual open competition for federal positions. The title alone does not say which overseas workers qualify or what conditions apply.

who_it_affects.group: Certain people who have worked overseas for the U.S. government
who_it_affects.how: Some of them may be able to get federal jobs without going through the normal competitive hiring process.
They may be allowed to hire these overseas workers directly instead of through open competition.
